Advertising is paid, non-personal messaging, public relations builds relationships and image, and personal selling involves direct interaction with a salesperson. A limited-time gift is a classic sales promotion tactic.
questions.hint: Short-term incentives to spur quick sales are sales promotion.
questions.learningObjective: identify elements of the promotional mix

options.misconception: mistakes a sales incentive for image-building communication
confuses a short-term incentive with paid mass messaging
assumes a face-to-face salesperson is required

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Redstone Bags, a established firm spends heavily on consumer advertising in Hillcrest so that buyers will ask retailers for the product, pulling it through the channel. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: A pull strategy directs promotion at final consumers to create demand that draws the product through the channel, so retailers stock it because customers ask for it. A push strategy instead aims promotion at intermediaries to get them to carry and sell the product. Consumer advertising that generates requests is the signature of a pull approach.
questions.hint: Demand created at the consumer end pulls the product forward.
questions.learningObjective: distinguish push from pull promotional strategies

options.misconception: assumes high initial prices define the channel approach
mistakes a channel approach for a pricing objective
confuses consumer demand generation with pushing goods to intermediaries

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: The Valemont Jewelry, a mid-sized firm team in Thornfield runs TV ads, social posts and in-store displays that each use a different slogan and colour scheme. What is the main weakness from an integrated marketing communications view?
questions.explanation: Integrated marketing communications aims for a consistent, coordinated message across all channels so that each exposure reinforces the others. When TV, social and in-store materials use different slogans and colours, the signals conflict and the brand image is diluted. The problem is not the number of media or any legal requirement, but the lack of a unified message.
questions.hint: Focus on whether all channels say the same thing.

options.misconception: assumes channels cannot work together

options.text: Using several media always lowers total reach
options.misconception: confuses a consistency problem with a reach problem

options.text: Inconsistent messages dilute the brand and confuse customers

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: A Larkspur Dairy, a national firm campaign in Redfern reaches 329,314 people with an average frequency of 2 exposures. How many total impressions does the campaign deliver?
questions.explanation: Impressions are the total number of exposures, equal to reach times average frequency. Here 329,314 people times 2 exposures gives 658,628 impressions. Adding the two figures would mix a headcount with an average, and reporting reach alone would ignore the repeat views that frequency captures. Reach and frequency together describe how widely and how often a message is seen.
questions.hint: Multiply the number of people reached by the average exposures each receives.

options.misconception: reports reach alone, ignoring repeat exposures
adds reach and frequency instead of multiplying them
divides reach by frequency
